name: CourseGlade LMS – Online Course & eLearning Platform
author: DevItems

sections.description:
CourseGlade LMS is a full-featured Learning Management System plugin for WordPress that helps you build, sell, and manage online courses from one place. Create courses with a drag-and-drop builder, support multiple instructors, deliver quizzes and multimedia lessons, manage students, accept payments, and provide a focused learning experience — all inside WordPress.

🎉 CourseGlade LMS is on AppSumo. Pay once and get lifetime access. See the AppSumo deal

👇 Helpful Links to Get Started

🔍 Learn More | 🚀 Explore Pro | 📘 Documentation | 💬 Support

Watch CourseGlade in Action

New in 2.0

  • A redesigned admin: every screen rebuilt, from the dashboard and course builder to students, orders, settings and tools
  • Fully translatable, admin and front end alike — run your whole academy in your own language
  • Course pages follow your catalogue page’s address, so a catalogue in another language gives every course a matching address, and old links redirect
  • A “My Courses” tab in WooCommerce’s My Account that opens the CourseGlade dashboard

Key Features

Build Courses Your Way

  • Drag-and-drop course builder with sections, lessons, and quizzes
  • Course categories, tags, and difficulty levels
  • Video lessons from YouTube, Vimeo, self-hosted files, or any oEmbed provider — one player for every source, and the lesson completes itself when the video ends
  • Audio lessons, with the same automatic completion when the track finishes
  • Course catalog with search, category filtering, and pagination

Create Engaging Learning Experiences

  • 8 quiz question types: multiple choice, single choice, true/false, fill in the blank, matching, ordering, short answer, and essay
  • Distraction-free learning mode with a curriculum drawer and progress tracking
  • Course reviews and discussion boards
  • Student dashboard with course progress and a wishlist
  • Custom avatar uploads, falling back to Gravatar

Sell Courses with Built-in Payment Options

  • Stripe, WooCommerce, Manual Payment, and Free (zero-price) gateways
  • Coupons and discounts
  • WooCommerce customers get a “My Courses” tab in their account
  • Free and paid course support
  • Transactional email notifications for enrolments, orders, course completion, and instructor applications

Manage Students and Instructors

  • Multi-instructor support with earnings and withdrawal management
  • Become-an-instructor application flow with admin approval
  • Public instructor profiles at /instructor/{username}/
  • Custom student and instructor roles with granular capabilities

Manage and Operate Your LMS

  • A modern admin for courses, students, instructors, orders, settings, and tools, with all settings on one screen and each credentials section saying where to find its keys
  • Export and import your settings, with a resumable job runner and an undo for an import that went wrong
  • A setup checklist on the dashboard, so a new site can see what is left to configure
  • Maintenance mode for your learning site
  • Shortcodes for course grids, dashboards, checkout, and authentication pages
  • Fully translation-ready, admin and front end (.pot included), and compatible with WordPress block themes

CourseGlade Pro — Premium Add-ons

CourseGlade Pro extends the free plugin with independently toggleable add-ons (requires the separate CourseGlade LMS Pro plugin):

  • Content Bank — one place for lessons, quizzes, questions, and assignments, shared between courses instead of copied, with random question sets for quizzes
  • Subscriptions & Memberships — sell recurring access to a course, a category, or your whole catalogue, with plans, trials, renewals, and cancellations
  • AI Studio — write any field from a brief, or generate a whole course: modules, lessons, quizzes with questions, and assignments. Bring your own API key
  • Certificates — auto-issue completion certificates with custom templates and shareable, verifiable certificate numbers
  • Assignments — file-upload assignments with instructor grading and feedback
  • Course Bundles — sell groups of courses together as a single product
  • Content Drip — release lessons and modules on a schedule or by enrolment date
  • Live Classes — schedule live sessions on a course, with attendance and per-instructor connections
  • Zoom — host live classes on Zoom; each instructor connects their own account
  • Google Meet — host live classes on Google Meet, with one site-level app and per-instructor consent
  • Gradebook — a per-student grade overview across quizzes and assignments
  • Leaderboard & Gamification — award points and badges, and rank learners
  • Advanced Reports — detailed revenue, enrolment, course, and instructor analytics
  • Advanced Email — broadcast campaigns, a send queue, and expanded notification events
  • Bulk Enrolment — enrol many students at once, or import them from a CSV
  • Social Login — let students sign in with Google, Facebook, or X
  • Import & Export (content) — move courses, lessons, quizzes, questions, curriculum, terms, and media between sites
  • Google Classroom — import and sync course rosters
  • White Label — rebrand the admin with your own name, logo, and colours

Source Code

The admin interface is built with React (Vite). The full, unminified source code is included in the plugin under assets/admin/src/. The compiled output is at assets/admin/build/.

To rebuild the admin assets:

  1. cd assets/admin
  2. npm install
  3. npm run build

External Services

This plugin connects to the following external services:

Stripe
Used to process course payments when the Stripe gateway is enabled. Checkout sessions are created against the Stripe API and the student is then redirected to Stripe’s own hosted checkout page to pay.
– Data sent: payment amount, currency, customer email, course details
– When sent: only during checkout when a student purchases a course
– Service URL: https://api.stripe.com (and Stripe’s hosted checkout at https://checkout.stripe.com)
– Terms of Service: https://stripe.com/legal
– Privacy Policy: https://stripe.com/privacy

Video embeds (YouTube, Vimeo)
Used to embed lesson videos when an instructor provides a YouTube or Vimeo video URL for a lesson. YouTube is embedded through youtube-nocookie.com. If an instructor instead chooses the “Embed” video source, WordPress’s built-in oEmbed fetches the markup from whichever provider the supplied URL belongs to, under that provider’s own terms and privacy policy.
– Data sent: standard browser request (IP address, browser info) when the video is loaded
– When sent: only when a student views a lesson that has a YouTube or Vimeo video URL set
– YouTube — Service URL: https://www.youtube-nocookie.com | Terms: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms | Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
– Vimeo — Service URL: https://vimeo.com | Terms: https://vimeo.com/terms | Privacy: https://vimeo.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the courseglade-lms folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install via the WordPress plugin installer.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to CourseGlade in the admin menu to complete setup.
  4. Configure payment gateways under CourseGlade → Settings → Payments.
sections.faq:
Does CourseGlade work with any WordPress theme?

Yes. CourseGlade includes its own frontend templates that work with any theme. Block-theme support is included.

What payment gateways are supported?

Stripe, WooCommerce, Manual payment, and Free (zero-price) enrolment are supported in the free version.

Do I need WooCommerce?

No. Stripe, Manual payment and Free enrolment work on their own. WooCommerce is one gateway of four, for sites that already sell through it and want courses in the same cart and order history.

Can I have multiple instructors?

Yes. You can invite instructors, set commission rates, and manage withdrawal requests from the admin.

Is the plugin translation-ready?

Yes, both halves of it. Everything your students see — course pages, the dashboard, checkout, emails — and every screen you work in as an administrator use the courseglade-lms text domain, and a .pot file covering all of it ships in languages/.

The easiest way to translate is the free Loco Translate plugin: install it, pick CourseGlade, and write your translation from inside WordPress. Poedit works too if you prefer a desktop tool. The admin interface is a JavaScript application, so after saving a .po file Loco Translate also needs to generate the matching .json files — it offers to do this, and the admin screens stay English until it has.

If you produce a translation we would be glad to ship it with the plugin and credit you. Send it to us through the contact link above.

Can I move my courses and settings to another site?

Settings, yes. Export them to a portable file and import it on the other site; the job resumes if it is interrupted, and an import that went wrong can be undone. Moving the content itself — courses, lessons, quizzes, questions, curriculum, terms and media — is part of CourseGlade LMS Pro.

Is there a Pro version?

Yes. CourseGlade LMS Pro adds Content Bank, Subscriptions & Memberships, AI Studio, Certificates, Assignments, Course Bundles, Content Drip, Live Classes with Zoom and Google Meet, Gradebook, Leaderboard & Gamification, Advanced Reports, Advanced Email, Bulk Enrolment, Social Login, content Import & Export, Google Classroom, and White Label. Each add-on can be enabled or disabled independently. The free plugin is fully functional on its own.
sections.changelog:
2.0.0

New
* A redesigned admin. Every screen has been rebuilt: dashboard, courses, students, instructors, orders, settings and tools.
* Course pages follow your catalogue page’s address, so a catalogue in another language gives every course a matching address. Old links redirect.
* WooCommerce: a My Courses tab in My Account that opens the CourseGlade dashboard.
* The admin and the front-end scripts are now translatable too. If you maintain a translation, the template now holds about 5,100 strings.

Improved
* Settings are one screen, and each credentials section says where to find its keys.
* Quiz attempts show and search by course; categories can have a thumbnail.
* Import and export History says what each job was, and each job can be acted on from it.
* A course’s progress counts only the content still in it.

Fixes
* “Days since active” no longer shows -1, and stored dates are read in the time zone they were written in.
* Removing content from a course follows one rule: with Content Bank it detaches, without it content nothing else uses is deleted.
* Many smaller fixes across the dashboard, withdrawals and quiz grading.

Security
* An empty email-verification token could sign a visitor in as another user who had not yet verified their email.
* A WooCommerce order could complete a course order it did not contain, so a cheap shop product unlocked a paid course.
* An instructor could take ownership of another instructor’s lesson through a course save.

1.2.4

Fixes
* Lesson lengths on the course page showed the wrong number.
* Module headings on the course page left out assignments.

1.2.3

Fixes
* Course URLs written in non-Latin scripts now display correctly in the editor, and stay editable.

1.2.2

Fixes
* Lessons and quizzes whose web address is not written in Latin letters — Bangla, Arabic, Chinese — open instead of returning nothing.
* A course access password is stored as it was typed, so an instructor can look it up and share it. Passwords already saved keep working.
* A private or password-protected course no longer wears a Featured badge or appears in a featured list.
* The lead instructor can no longer be removed from their own course in one step: hand the course to someone else first, and a course always has an owner.

Improved
* A course card says when more than one person teaches it.
* Quizzes and assignments are told apart at a glance in the curriculum, each with its own colour and label.

1.2.1

Fixes
* Fixed duplicate courses being created when switching tabs in the course editor.

1.2.0

New
* A redesigned front end. The catalogue, course page, checkout, learning area, quiz player and instructor profile have been rebuilt on one set of design tokens.
* The student dashboard has been rebuilt, with a new Activity tab and a printable invoice for every order.
* Category, level and price filters on the course grid.
* Instructor profiles have their own reviews page, and sites can word what an instructor’s years of experience mean.
* Sign-in and registration have been rebuilt, and the become-an-instructor application with them.
* The course grid takes shortcode attributes: choose which filters appear, hide individual ones, and set what each starts on.
* Four more ways to sort a catalogue — most popular, top rated, and price in either direction.

Improved
* Q&A threads open in place, with helpful votes and a best answer. Q&A on a quiz is now opt-in per quiz, off by default.
* Course progress is summarised on the enrolment row, so a dashboard of many courses is no longer many queries.
* Withdrawals can be cancelled while pending, name the destination they will be paid to, and explain a rejection.
* Most of the plugin’s text is newly translatable. If you maintain a translation, around 700 strings are newly available — the previous template was missing the whole student and instructor dashboard.

Fixes
* Quiz answer review marked every option as the student’s answer on some question types.
* Courses are now attributed to the instructor who teaches them. A course an administrator created and handed over stayed authored by the administrator, so anything that asked WordPress whose course it was got the wrong answer.
* A page using a feature from an addon that is switched off no longer prints the shortcode’s own syntax at customers.
* Subscription and membership settings no longer take effect when nothing is installed that can sell them.
* Live class times are shown in the reader’s own timezone rather than the server’s, and a host can end a session early.
* Manual payments require their instructions to be filled in. A payout control that wrote nowhere has been removed.
* Import and export work on Windows. Every job failed with “Invalid file path” on WAMP, XAMPP and IIS, because the plugin compared its own folder against itself using the wrong kind of slash.
* A newly published course no longer goes missing from the Top rated sort.
* Smaller fixes to the wishlist, the catalogue’s level filter, instructor visibility in Q&A, and who may export.

Security
* Escaping, input sanitising and prepared statements were reviewed across the plugin against the WordPress coding standards.

1.1.0

New
* Audio lessons. Add an audio track to a lesson and it plays in the learning area, with the lesson completing itself when the track finishes.
* One player for every video source. Self-hosted, YouTube and Vimeo lessons now share the same controls, and a lesson marks itself complete when the video reaches the end — which YouTube and Vimeo lessons previously never did.
* Export and import. Move settings between sites as a portable file, with a job runner that resumes where it left off and can undo an import that went wrong.
* A setup checklist on the dashboard, so a new site can see what is left to configure.

Fixes
* An unexpected error during checkout no longer fails as a blank page. Requests that go wrong now return a proper error the site can act on, instead of a PHP fatal that could also print server paths when error display is switched on.
* Instructor invitations work. The acceptance link was broken, and accepting one did not finish setting the account up.
* A video lesson could not be saved in some cases.

1.0.2

New & improved
* Course pages now use your theme’s fonts. The plugin no longer forces its own font family on the frontend, so changing fonts in your theme or global styles takes effect everywhere.

Fixes
* The course builder now sends the course along with content drip requests, so drip rules can be set on a lesson while it is still being created.

1.0.1

Security
* Restricted the enrollment REST endpoints to administrators (were reachable with an instructor-level capability).
* Escaped instructor-application data returned by the REST API.
* Closed several per-course ownership gaps and stopped quiz endpoints exposing answer keys.
* Added login throttling; the instructor user-picker now searches by name only and no longer exposes emails.

New & improved
* Course cards show the instructor’s avatar linked to their public profile.
* Maintenance mode now also covers the course archive and category/tag/difficulty pages, with a new filter to adjust its scope.
* Real avatars now appear in quiz grading, submissions, and order details.

Fixes
* Scheduled maintenance tasks (cache cleanup, stale-order cancellation, enrollment expiry, stats refresh) now actually run on cron.
* Made order and withdrawal status transitions atomic to prevent duplicate processing.
* Blocked creating a duplicate order while one is still pending for the same course.
* Numerous settings, learning-mode, and responsive-layout fixes.

Performance
* Removed N+1 queries from the instructor and order lists and batched dashboard revenue calculations.
* Per-order options are no longer autoloaded on every request.

1.0.0

  • Initial release
